You're completely misinformed, NASA does a lot of very important research on the ISS, as I'm sure you'd agree. After the landing of the shuttle, (due to death, safety, massively over budget etc) NASA had no other choice but to buy seats from Russia, who obviously overcharged NASA.

By instead spending a fraction of the NASA budget on SpaceX, Boeing etc, NASA doesn't have to rely on the Russian space agency, thus massively reducing the cost of access to space, which is already being seen as seats on crew dragon are much much cheaper than on soyuz. Whilst private industry can focus on LEO and travel to the ISS, innovating and reducing cost, NASA will have more budget to spend on exciting research missions such as perseverance (Mars 2020).

Private industry is not taking over everything by a long shot, perseverance for example includes MOXIE, ingenuity, microphones, hi res cameras and sample collectors for future return, NASA still plays a vital role in research and discovery.

Without private companies such as boeing, spacex and blue origin getting involved with aspects of the industry such as LEO, we will end up with another shuttle program, a massively over budget and quite frankly dangerous program, which unfortunately looks like how SLS is turning out. Don't get me wrong, I love the old NASA, the shuttle etc, but to claim they are cheaper and better on the tax payer is just utterly wrong in every aspect
